Perhaps when a Nobody writes notes to themselves, they leave them in places other Nobodies will find them, and only Nobodies will notice them unless they want someone like a Foundation agent to find it or V. Anderson. Or the Nobodies just have an information network that's so average and normal, no one but other Nobodies truly notice it? Talking and exchanging notes at a coffee shop, in a park on a bench, at a cafe or even just out and about.

item.title: Proposed Alternative to the Format
item.content:encoded:
This is not to suggest a replacement; just an alternative to use.

Thanks to the work of anqxyr and Aiden Eldritch, you can get a format that's more stylistically sleek and easier to work with for the end user, as well as being able to write more per page and insert images easier. The downside is that the text will rarely if ever align with the lines neatly, meaning readability can be a potential issue. And while on mobile, it's extremely legible (minus the notebook/paper background which is absent), it also takes up a ton of screen space except for viewing it on Landscape mode. Here is the code:

+ show block
– hide block
 [!--The following is the CSS for which the format will rely on. This cuts out the need of constant rows and cells. --] [[module css]] .page { display: block; overflow: hidden; font-family: "Monotype Corsiva", "Bradley Hand ITC", sans-serif; font-style: italic; width: 46%; background-attachment: scroll; background-clip: border-box; background-color: transparent; background-image: -moz-linear-gradient(center top , rgb(202, 219, 228) 0%, rgb(231, 233, 220) 8%); background-origin: padding-box; background-position: 0px 4px; background-repeat: repeat; background-size: 100% 20px; height: 450px; border: 1px solid #CCC; border-radius: 10px; padding: 0px 10px; margin-bottom: 10px; box-shadow: 0px 1px 3px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2) } .left { float: left; } .right { float: right; } [[/module]] [[div class="page left"]] [!--Line 1 starts here like so. --] __**Title of Object goes here**__ [!--The @@ @@ aborts Wikidot parsing. Wikidot takes away whitespaces, but by using @@ @@, it can force such a thing to allow for paragraph breaks, because Wikidot will read the space in there and include it instead of taking it away if you use too many. Here, we use it to try and aide in readability. --] @@ @@ [!--Second line goes here like so. --] __Aliases__: Aliases go here. @@ @@ __Summary__: Paragraphs can be as long as you want, so long as you don't write such long paragraphs or too many paragraphs for one page. With this alternative format, you can fit more text onto one note, opening up possible narrative options. @@ @@ One thing the original format does extremely well is force you to write with brevity in mind and try to be as concise, useful, and impactful as possible. That said, this still conveys that same spirit. After all, you don't have to use the whole page. [[/div]] [[div class="page right"]] [!--Typically, you're going to want two pages to include any potent information, considering the format is broken up into three main categories. --] __Threat__: This is such a second page. @@ @@ [!--If you want to include an image in your thing, there's no need to make a new table for images; you just need to upload the image to the page, include the code below (either as a link or as the filename; in this case, Decibelleisthebest.png. This should be its own line. --] [[f>image http://scpsandbox2.wdfiles.com/local--files/decibelle-one-half/Decibelleisthebest.png width="90px"]] @@ @@ The rest of the text can then proceed as normal. An example of what an image in this format can look like is found as a link below. @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ Bottom text. [[/div]]

An example of what this looks like sans image is here. An example of what this looks like with image is here.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: There are infinitely better ways of creating pseudo-lined text with the intent of making it look like handwritten notes; most importantly, it's possible to do without having to resort to things like manually controlling the length of each line, which is untenable for reuse and doesn't parse well. I would recommend talking to someone with some expertise in web design next time, or at least cleaning it up after the contest is over.

item.title: Changes and Uploads

Any thoughts are welcome, and as always, thank you for reading.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Alright, now that this is actually following the rules of the contest, critique. This is just repeating what I said on IRC, so bear with me.

The bad: This is overly long, repetitive, and a bit doofy (sorry Sorts) in parts. Some elements are unnecessarily confusing.

The good: I think your core concept is surprisingly strong. You've got some cool lines. When Nobody's letter finally gets down to brass tacks, I find myself intrigued. This bit in particular:

Here at last is an answer I can give without imprecision. I am not whole in the way that others are. I am not significant in the way that others are. I am unable to affect the world in the way others are.

I read that and I think, okay, I'm actually interested to see what this is all about.

It might not end up going well — as I said, there's a balance here between stuff that bores me and stuff that intrigues me — but as it stands, it's enough for an upvote for the front material at least.

Man, Dr Hockenberry, I really wish you had discussed this with me before posting -_-

I fixed the format to match the GOI Contest format, and added my own writing to the Overview and Information tabs. At this time both these are still fairly rough, as I wasn't planning on posting anything this early. However, I'd rather something there than just a blank page. As far as the Information tab goes, I will probably add more when I get a chance.

Any feedback would be appreciated, as I haven't yet had the chance to seek it out previously. Especially grammar, spacing, and wording fixes, as those can be edited during the contest. More extensive critique is also appreciated, though that will have to wait for after the contest (if this manages to survive afterwards).

As always, thanks for reading. I'm excited to see what comes out of this contest, and wish all the participants the best of luck.
